name: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Musnadi
nameAr: عبد الله بن محمد بن عبد الله بن جعفر بن اليمان الجعفي، أبو جعفر، البخاري، المعروف بالمسندي

orthography.spelled: al-Musnadi, with fathah on the nun

taqrib.en: Reliable, a hadith master; he compiled the Musnad.

role: Teacher of al-Bukhari; compiler of a Musnad

verdicts.en: Listed in al-Thiqat: he was precise.

verdicts.ar: كان أبو جعفر المسندي غاب عن بلده وأقام في طلب الحديث في الآفاق، وكان يلقب بالمسندي، وهو من المعروفين من أهل العدالة والصدق، صاحب سنة وجماعة، عرف بالإتقان والضبط
verdicts.en: Abu Ja'far al-Musnadi left his town and stayed abroad seeking hadith; he was nicknamed al-Musnadi, and is among the well-known men of integrity and truthfulness, a man of the Sunnah, known for precision and exactness.

verdicts.ar: سمي المسندي لأنه أول من جمع مسند الصحابة بما وراء النهر، وهو إمام الحديث في عصره هناك بلا مدافعة
verdicts.en: He was called al-Musnadi because he was the first to compile the Musnad of the Companions beyond the Oxus; he was the undisputed imam of hadith of his age in that region.

dhahabi.source: al-Kashif, as given on the Shamela record

flags.label: A muhmal name
flags.detail: Al-Bukhari writes only “Abdullah ibn Muhammad”, a name shared by several of his teachers, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah among them. Ibn Hajar: where the name is unqualified it means al-Ju'fi, because al-Bukhari was especially attached to him and narrated from him a great deal (Fath al-Bari on 4663).

flags.label: Claim not verified
flags.detail: The class notes say his ancestor al-Yaman al-Ju'fi was the man through whom al-Bukhari's grandfather al-Mughirah accepted Islam, which is why al-Bukhari too carries the nisba al-Ju'fi. The Shamela record notes only that al-Yaman ibn Akhnas is “one of al-Bukhari's forebears from above”; the story itself was not verified here.

bio: A Bukharan who travelled widely for hadith and came home to compile the first Musnad of the Companions in Transoxiana, which gave him his laqab. Al-Bukhari drew on him in many places and names him only as Abdullah ibn Muhammad; al-Tirmidhi is the only other of the six to use him. He is the lower link that makes al-Bukhari's route to Hammam in hadith 4663 a step longer than the two routes beside it.

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari on hadith 4663 (islamweb)
